hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when you’ve made a mistake, what’s harder for you: saying sorry, or forgiving yourself?
options: honest answer. today’s story makes it a little easier.
that’s a hard one. today might help.
then you’re in good company. listen.

steps.line: After the whisper, Adam and his wife stood in the garden, covered in leaves. And their Lord called to them.
This was their fork in the road. Remember Iblis? When he was sent away, he blamed God: “Because You led me astray.”

steps.q: What do you think Adam and his wife said?
o: “Our Lord, forgive us; we didn’t know”
steps.why: No excuse, no blame, not even ignorance. Just the truth (7:23).

steps.line: They said: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You don’t forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be lost.”

steps.q: In the Qur’an, who does the whisperer go to?
o: Both of them, never her alone
Adam alone, and he tells her
steps.why: Satan whispered to them both (7:20), and one passage speaks to Adam by name (20:120). The Qur’an never puts the slip on her alone.

steps.line: Then Adam received words from his Lord, the Qur’an says, and God turned toward him. He is the One who keeps turning, the Merciful.

steps.q: In Islam, does Adam’s mistake pass down to his children?
o: Yes, everyone is born carrying it
No, it was forgiven and ends with him
Only for people who never repent
steps.why: The Qur’an says no soul carries another’s burden (6:164). Muslims see every child born with fitra, a clean, good nature.

steps.line: A saying adds a picture: God is happier at a person’s return than a traveler who lost his camel in the desert, then finds it standing right there.

steps.q: In the full saying, the man is so overjoyed to find his camel that he gets his words backwards. What comes out?
o: “God, You are my servant, and I am Your Lord!”
steps.why: Sahih Muslim tells it: he blurts it out from sheer joy, and isn’t blamed. God’s joy at a person’s return, the Prophet ﷺ said, is greater still.

steps.line: Today, a mistake lands, and it’s clearly yours. One way out: explain. The other: three hard words. I was wrong.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. adam didn’t make a speech. he said, we did wrong, please forgive us. and God turned toward him.

in islam, adam was forgiven, and no soul carries another’s load, so no one is born carrying his mistake. tawbah means turning back, and God is at-tawwab, the One who turns back to you, again and again.

steps.q: Tawbah is a person turning to God; at-Tawwab is God turning to the person. Same root. What does that suggest?
o: Every turn back is met by a turn toward you
You have to earn forgiveness first
steps.why: You take a step back, and you’re met. Like the traveler and his camel, with joy.

today.say: today, say three hard words about one small thing: “i was wrong.” to a friend, a partner, a coworker, or quietly to God. many muslims say astaghfirullah, i ask God’s forgiveness, through the day. it’s your choice.
options: lovely. that’s the way back, every time.
beautiful. a small word for turning back.

Qur’an 7:16 (Iblis: “Now, because Thou hast sent me astray…”)

Commentators who identify the “words” of 2:37 with 7:23: e.g. al-Tabari on 2:37
